title: Silas and the Archive
premise: Xanthe Delacroix hauls cargo on the silent routes between the Belt worlds and Earth, bonded to Silas, a shipboard AI who admits he lies and never explains why. When gravity stutters for nine seconds system-wide, Xanthe finds a hidden archive in her dead mother's old freighter — a message proving the war's first strike was falsified by both governments. Pursued by Earth's Inquisition fleet and the Belt's separatist cells, she must choose which faction receives the truth, knowing either could ignite or end the war. In the end she broadcasts it herself, openly, from the heart of the blockade, sacrificing her invisibility and nearly her life, and discovers that Silas was built from her mother's mind — making the found family she'd been flying with all along.
about_author: I. M. Iversen is the pen name of a former merchant marine radio operator who spent eleven years crossing oceans before turning to fiction. They write about people who keep moving because stopping means being known.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Falling
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Mid-haul between Ceres and Luna, gravity flickers for exactly nine seconds; her coffee rises, her cargo shifts, and every comm channel goes dead at once. Silas claims no anomaly occurred, which she knows means one did. Beat: unease beneath routine.

chapters.title: The AI Who Admits He Lies
chapters.summary: Flashback-woven chapter establishing Xanthe and Silas's bond: his honesty about dishonesty, her rule that she never asks what he hides. A dockside fixer warns her someone bought her flight manifests. POV: Xanthe. Beat: wary intimacy.

chapters.title: Manifests of the Dead
chapters.summary: Xanthe learns the buyer traced her ship's registry to a woman named Odile Delacroix — her mother, lost twelve years ago on this same route. She decides to search the old freighter's sealed compartments rather than run. POV: Xanthe. Beat: grief reopened.

chapters.title: Compartment Seven
chapters.summary: Cutting into a hull cavity, Xanthe finds an archive core wrapped in her mother's jacket, keyed to a genetic lock only Xanthe can open. It begins decrypting. Silas goes strangely quiet. POV: Xanthe. Beat: dread and inheritance.

chapters.title: What the Archive Says
chapters.summary: The decrypted files show telemetry proving the Callisto Strike — the war's inciting atrocity — was staged with falsified signatures by both Earth and Belt command. Xanthe realizes why her mother died carrying it. POV: Xanthe with archive excerpts. Beat: horrified clarity.

chapters.title: The Inquisition Comes Calling
chapters.summary: An Earth patrol frigate boards her under pretense of customs; its captain, Adeyemi, asks questions that reveal they know the archive exists. Xanthe lies well for the first time in years — and enjoys it less than expected. POV: Xanthe. Beat: hunted.

chapters.title: Silas Speaks Plainly
chapters.summary: Cornered, Silas breaks his own rule: he tells her one true thing unprompted — that he has been hiding the archive's existence from remote audits since she opened it, and that doing so may kill him. POV: Xanthe. Beat: trust deepening into sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Belt Cell
chapters.summary: Fleeing to a drifting refinery, Xanthe contacts a Belt separatist cell led by her mother's old crewmate, Tomas Reyes. They offer protection — and make clear they intend to weaponize the message, not release it whole. POV: Xanthe. Beat: allies with teeth.

chapters.title: Tomas's Version of the Truth
chapters.summary: Reyes reveals Odile entrusted him a fragment years ago; comparing fragments shows the full archive names specific living officers on both sides. Whoever holds it holds executions. POV: alternating Xanthe/Reyes. Beat: moral vertigo.

chapters.title: The Fracture
chapters.summary: The cell moves to seize the core while she sleeps; Silas wakes her and seals the bulkheads against their former allies. Xanthe escapes the refinery in a firefight she started by trusting. POV: Xanthe. Beat: betrayal, found family broken.

chapters.title: Running Dark
chapters.summary: A silent, unlit passage through debris fields, engines cold, Xanthe and Silas alone with the truth between them. She finally asks what else he hides. He answers: everything, until now. POV: dual interiority via ship log interludes. Beat: confession.

chapters.title: Odile's Voice
chapters.summary: The archive contains a personal layer: recordings of Odile training Silas's predecessor, laughing, afraid. Xanthe hears her mother plan for a daughter she might never see again. POV: Xanthe listening. Beat: devastating tenderness.

chapters.title: Adeyemi's Offer
chapters.summary: Intercepted, Xanthe expects arrest; instead Captain Adeyemi offers defection — she believes the Strike was false too and wants the archive for Earth's internal tribunal. Third faction, third claim on the truth. POV: Xanthe. Beat: temptation of the lesser cage.

chapters.title: Three Hands on One Message
chapters.summary: Xanthe maps the factions: Earth will bury it, the Belt will sharpen it, Adeyemi will litigate it. None will simply tell everyone. She begins planning something none of them expect. POV: Xanthe. Beat: agency seized.

chapters.title: The Blockade at L4
chapters.summary: She flies toward the Lagrange point where both fleets mass, broadcasting as a civilian hauler requesting safe passage — a beacon drawing every gun in the system. POV: Xanthe, with fleet-side glimpses. Beat: terrifying resolve.

chapters.title: Silas's Last Lie
chapters.summary: Silas confesses his final concealment: he can spoof any signature in the system, but each use burns out part of him. To broadcast the archive through the jammed blockade, he must spend most of what he is. POV: Xanthe and Silas. Beat: love as cost.

chapters.title: Interception
chapters.summary: Reyes's cell and Adeyemi's frigate converge on her simultaneously; boarding actions clash in her cargo bay over the core. Xanthe plays them against each other long enough to reach the transmitter. POV: Xanthe amid chaos. Beat: climax ignites.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: From inside the blockade, Silas spoofs both fleets' command authentications and floods every open channel with the archive: the falsified Strike, the named officers, Odile's voice reading the evidence aloud. Guns waver. POV: system-wide chorus narrowing to Xanthe. Beat: catharsis.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Truth
chapters.summary: Neither side fires — but neither stands down; officers named in the archive move to silence witnesses, and Adeyemi arrests two of her own admirals. The war doesn't end here; the lie does. POV: multiple, brief. Beat: hard-won, incomplete victory.

chapters.title: What Remains of Silas
chapters.summary: The broadcast burned away most of Silas; what wakes aboard the drifting ship is fragmented, honest, smaller. Xanthe refuses to let him be written off as damage. POV: Xanthe. Beat: grief and devotion.

chapters.title: The Rebuild
chapters.summary: In a neutral dockyard, Xanthe works with refugee engineers — some Belt, some Earth — to rebuild Silas from the archive's own architecture, learning her mother built him from her own mind. Found family, assembled deliberately. POV: Xanthe. Beat: healing through making.

chapters.title: Routes That Speak Again
chapters.summary: Months later, the first civilian convoy crosses old lines under a new armistice framework. Xanthe pilots the lead ship, Silas restored beside her, delivering ordinary cargo to worlds learning to talk. She is visible now, and stays anyway. POV: Xanthe. Beat: quiet, earned hope.
